summary: Initial security posture review focusing on hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs. Main customer concerns: KMS integration, SSO/SAML + SCIM for RBAC, audit logging granularity, and data retention for EU customers. Redwood AE/SE committed to sharing SOC2 artifacts and running a technical deep dive on private options.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-13 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46m
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Elysium Head Eng), Marcus Lee (Elysium Security Lead), Hannah Cho (Platform), Omar Nazir (CTO)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time. Quick roll call then we'll jump in. I'm Maya Chen, account exec on the Redwood side, and with me is Diego Alvarez, our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Priya: Hi, Priya here.
[00:14] Marcus: Marcus Lee.
[00:16] Hannah: Hannah.
[00:17] Omar: Omar here.
[00:19] Diego: Hey all. 

[00:25] Maya: High level agenda, we want to understand your security playbook and constraints, talk through hosting options — hosted, dedicated, private — and surface any must-haves like SSO, KMS, audit logs. We'll note next steps and artifacts. Sound good?
[00:35] Priya: Yep. We're mainly trying to decide if our initial rollout can be Redwood hosted or if we need dedicated or private from day one because of PCI and EU data residency.

[00:50] Marcus: To add — SOC2 is a requirement for us, and we need to know if you guys have continuous monitoring, audit log retention for 1 year, and tamper-proof logs. Also curious about encryption key control — BYOK or bring-your-own-key, and HSM compatibility.
[01:10] Diego: Yeah, great. So quick note — Redwood's hosted offering has SOC2 Type II, we can share the report, and we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations. On HSM, there is an integration path with major cloud KMSes, and for private we can support on-prem HSM as part of the package.
[01:30] Marcus: When you say KMS integration, do you support rotation policies from our side or is it managed by Redwood? We need to ensure we can rotate keys monthly and have audit trail of key usage.
[01:44] Diego: We support both managed and customer-managed models. For hosted you can do cloud KMS where Redwood calls the key via a policy; rotation can be automated per your KMS settings. For Dedicated there's more isolation and for Private you get full BYOK with a KMS tunnel. Apologies if I say K V cache earlier, that's internal.
[02:05] Hannah: OK, interesting. On SSO — we require SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning, ideally SCIM v2 for user groups and RBAC. Can you confirm?
[02:16] Maya: Short answer: yes. Redwood supports SSO via SAML and OIDC; SCIM provisioning is supported for automatic user + group sync. Diego, want to add on roles?
[02:26] Diego: Sure. Our product supports role-based access controls — prebuilt roles and custom roles. SCIM maps groups to roles, and audit logs capture admin changes. Small caveat — the hosted path ties into Redwood's identity plane; for private we can integrate directly with your IdP over a VPN. Sometimes our transcription says s s o slash s a m l which is funny.
[02:48] Marcus: That caveat matters — we can't have a middleman for auth for some EU-regulated datasets.
[02:55] Omar: Can you run through what the audit logs contain? We need user-level actions, model invocations, token redaction evidence, and config changes with timestamps and origin IP.
[03:06] Diego: Logs include request-level metadata (timestamp, user id, route, model, latency), admin events (role changes, key rotations), and system events (deployments, rollbacks). We include IP and region, though IP may be at the gateway in hosted. Also, we can provide immutable storage export to your S3 for long term retention in the private/dedicated contracts.
[03:29] Priya: How long are logs retained by default in hosted? We saw something about 90 days in a doc but need 12 months for audits.
[03:36] Maya: Hosted default is 90 days for detailed request logs, aggregated metrics longer. If you need 12 months we can set a retention add-on or put a flow that exports to your S3. For Dedicated/Private retention policies can be configured per contract.
[03:51] Marcus: Okay that's acceptable if export is supported. Regarding data at rest, is everything encrypted with customer keys or Redwood-managed keys?
[03:59] Diego: We encrypt at rest and in transit. For hosted the default uses Redwood-managed KMS; we offer customer-managed KMS via cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). For Private, you can bring an HSM or on-prem KMS. There are some limits on certain caching layers where we use envelope encryption — but keys are customer-controlled if BYOK is configured.
[04:23] Priya: We need to validate that the KV caching layer doesn't leak PII in logs. Can you confirm whether cache keys or partial prompts are written to logs?
[04:33] Diego: Good question. We avoid logging raw prompt content. Caching metadata may be logged for performance debugging, but payloads are redacted. We'll share the exact redaction policy in the security pack.
[04:45] Hannah: Also, we have a firewall and egress rules; any hosted deployment needs to support IP whitelisting or private link.
[04:53] Maya: Hosted supports VPC peering and private link with supported cloud providers; Dedicated has network isolation and private endpoints; Private is fully customer controlled.
[05:03] Marcus: On compliance, besides SOC2, do you have ISO27001?
[05:07] Diego: We maintain ISO alignment — I think we have ISO 27001 certification for the core control plane; I'll confirm and send the certs.
[05:16] Omar: For EU data residency — we need processing to happen in EU regions. Does your hosted platform allow region pinning?
[05:24] Maya: Yes, we have region routing and can pin requests to EU regions for Enterprise customers; if you need strict data residency for regulated datasets we typically recommend Dedicated in-region or Private deployment.
[05:36] Priya: Talk to me about model artifacts and storage. We build custom fine-tuned models. Will Redwood store our model binaries and are those encrypted?
[05:45] Diego: We can host model artifacts encrypted at rest; they can be stored in a customer-owned bucket for Private/Dedicated and we can mount or point to them. For hosted there's an option to store in Redwood managed storage with customer-managed key for encryption. We can arrange a gated pipeline so model binaries are only accessible to the serving runtime.
[06:06] Marcus: Do you have separation between customer tenants at the storage layer? We need multi-tenant isolation assurances.
[06:12] Diego: Yes, multi-tenant isolation by default in hosted — logical separation, RBAC, and least privilege. Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools and storage segments. Private is fully isolated.
[06:23] Priya: Another concern — retention of user prompts and generated outputs. We need to retain conversational logs for 6 months for our support and compliance and then purge. How flexible is that?
[06:33] Maya: We can enable data retention windows per dataset or route. Hosted default may have limitations but we provide export and purge hooks. Dedicated and Private give you full control.
[06:42] Hannah: Encryption in transit — do you support mutual TLS between Redwood runtime and our internal services?
[06:49] Diego: Mutual TLS is supported for private endpoints and for dedicated with private link; for public hosted endpoints we enforce TLS 1.2/1.3 with cert pinning options.
[06:59] Omar: On monitoring — we need SIEM integration, log forwarding to Splunk/Datadog. Is that available?
[07:05] Maya: Yes, we have integrations for log forwarding and webhook sinks. We'll include details.

[07:20] Marcus: Let's talk threat model briefly. Our main risk is exfiltration of PII via model outputs or logs. How do you prevent that?
[07:29] Diego: There's a few layers: redaction at ingestion, output filters, and an allowlist/denylist for outputs. Also, we can set up evals and quality monitors that trigger alerts if PII patterns are detected. Those are part of Redwood Optimize/Quality hooks — excuse me if I conflate internal names.
[07:50] Priya: We might want on-call hooks into your incident process — SLA for incident response and security contacts.
[07:57] Maya: Enterprise contracts include an incident response SLA, designated security contact, and quarterly security reviews.

[08:10] Marcus: One operational question — for Dedicated, how does autoscaling affect network egress and audit trails? If nodes scale up, do we see identities mapped correctly in logs?
[08:20] Diego: Yes, scaled nodes inherit the same tenant identity mapping. We maintain a request ID that ties to the original user and route, so horizontal scaling doesn't break traceability. Logs include the instance id and request id.

[08:35] Priya: I'd like to understand the upgrade/patch cadence. If you're rolling out runtime changes, how are we notified and do we get canary rollouts?
[08:43] Diego: We do staged rollouts with canaries; Dedicated/Private customers can opt into maintenance windows. We'll share the release cadence doc.

[08:55] Maya: Quick poll — is your preference leaning toward hosted for speed of prototyping or do the compliance constraints already push you to dedicated/private?
[09:03] Omar: Prototype could be hosted but for production with EU PCI data, we think dedicated in-region is likely.
[09:12] Marcus: Agreed. We want to pilot a small set of non-PII flows on hosted to test latency and costs, then move regulated routes to Dedicated.
[09:21] Priya: If we do that, can we pin model versions so the hosted prototype and dedicated production use the same model semantics?
[09:27] Diego: You can pin model versions and rollout policies across environments — that's a core pattern we recommend to avoid regressions.

[09:36] Hannah: A tiny nit — do you have token-level billing that we can attribute to routes for internal cost allocation?
[09:42] Maya: Yes, we provide token-level breakdowns per route and per API key. That helps chargeback.

[09:50] Marcus: Are there any hard limits we should be aware of — max sequence length, concurrency per user, or KV cache size?
[09:58] Diego: Limits exist but are tunable; sequence length depends on the model. Concurrency tiers are tied to Dedicated capacity. We'll send a performance profile for models you plan to use.

[10:10] Omar: Let's set timeline expectations — we want POC in 6 weeks and production in 4 months if things go well.
[10:18] Maya: Sounds reasonable. We'll propose a POC scope after this call.

[10:25] Priya: Can you send references of customers who've done hybrid hosted-to-dedicated migrations?
[10:30] Maya: Yes, we'll include a reference list and case studies.

[10:36] Marcus: Back to audit logs — do you support append-only tamper evidence? We need logs that are append-only for forensic purposes.
[10:45] Diego: We can push logs to your external immutable storage (e.g., S3 with object lock) to achieve append-only guarantees. Hosted by default doesn't have object-lock enabled unless configured.

[10:58] Hannah: For SCIM — do you support group-scoped provisioning and automatic deprovisioning?
[11:05] Diego: Yes. Groups can be mapped to roles and deprovisioning removes access and can trigger session revocation.

[11:15] Priya: About session revocation — if we remove a user, do you invalidate tokens immediately?
[11:20] Diego: We have session TTLs, and we support immediate revocation for SSO sessions in dedicated/private integrations via the IdP hooks. Hosteds can be near-real-time depending on the provider.

[11:33] Maya: I want to call out costs tradeoff — Private has the highest operational overhead but lowest risk for data residency and control. Dedicated is middle ground — isolated capacity with Redwood ops. Hosted is fastest and most cost-efficient for non-regulated loads.
[11:49] Marcus: Understood. We'll want a TCO comparison in your POC proposal.

[12:00] Omar: Any known limitations for GDPR Right to Erasure requests? Can you delete all user data on request across caches and backups?
[12:10] Diego: We support erasure workflows; we can scrub primary data and provide evidence. Backups are trickier — we can implement retention and purge policies, but you should plan a data retention window that meets GDPR processes. We'll document the end-to-end erasure capabilities.

[12:28] Priya: Can we get a copy of your pen test summary and vulnerability management processes?
[12:33] Maya: Yes, we'll share pen test summaries appropriate for NDA customers; otherwise we'll share a redacted summary.

[12:40] Marcus: How do you handle secrets in CI/CD for model deployments? We require ephemeral credentials or vault-based flows.
[12:48] Diego: We support keyed service accounts, ephemeral tokens via vault integrations, and don't bake secrets into images. For Private we can integrate with your vault.

[13:00] Hannah: For the POC, what would you need from us?
[13:05] Maya: Ideally a small dataset (non-PII), an example prompt set, and a list of routes to instrument. For security we'll ask for a POC scoping doc and a contact for Marcus for security checks.

[13:20] Marcus: We'll also provide a short inventory of regulated data types and the retention windows.

[13:27] Diego: One small note — when we say 'audit logs capture request body' we mean metadata by default; bodies are redacted. If you need bodies stored, that's a config with retention and redaction controls.
[13:42] Priya: Noted. That helps.

[13:48] Maya: Any other blockers we didn't cover?
[13:51] Omar: No, just need the SOC2 and KMS spec. Also sample network diagram for Dedicated.

[14:00] Maya: Great. We'll send the SOC2, sample network diagram, list of endpoints, and a proposed POC scope. Diego will lead the technical deep dive next week.
[14:10] Priya: On timing, next week is tight for Marcus, maybe the week after?
[14:15] Diego: Week after works, happy to schedule.

[14:20] Maya: Recap of next steps — share SOC2 and security pack, Diego to prep private/dedicated checklist and network diagrams, customer to provide PII inventory and retention policy. We'll propose POC scope and TCO.

[14:40] Marcus: Thanks, that seems good.
[14:42] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with a calendar hold for the deep dive.
[14:46] (end of recorded conversation)

Notes on transcription: occasional label errors and filler words; several technical terms may be slightly mis-transcribed ("KV cache" sometimes spaced, "SOC2" transcribed as "sock two" in parts).
